role: author implementation and bounded verification; not independent review of own implementation

api.prepare: IdeaLake.prepare_proposal: same insert metadata normalization, no database operation, default status queued; no admission capability.
api.caller_owned: admit_proposal_in_tx(lake, prepared): existing caller transaction required; no BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/PRAGMA/SAVEPOINT; normal exact-ID/orphan/dedup/new-row policy.
api.failure: ProposalAdmissionError propagates partial-write failure; caller must roll back the whole composed writer.
api.result_authority: All returned outcomes are transaction-local/provisional. In particular inserted is not a durable ACK. The outer coordinator must validate its complete write set and read committed state before acknowledgment.
api.writer_mode: BEGIN IMMEDIATE is a caller precondition, not something sqlite3.Connection.in_transaction can prove. No hidden lock upgrade is performed.
api.compatibility: Old insert(if_absent=True) still rejects caller transactions and owns its original transaction/error-return semantics. Legacy default insert remains INSERT OR REPLACE with None return. Replica private _new_rows remains distinct and is never the normal-admission entry.
api.temp_scope: Composable helper rejects case-insensitive TEMP table/view aliases of the five main admission tables; it does not introduce a second catalog.

limitations: This helper does not itself commit or provide a source acknowledgment. Coordinator-level request/outcome/source fences and commit uncertainty belong to the new coordinator, not to this local result dictionary.
No normal-proposal duplicate exemption was introduced. CPU versus non-CPU grouping and admitted-status policy are unchanged; non-CPU kinds are not silently split into separate dedup categories.
The normalizer and legacy insertion body were statically compared, and the relevant old tests were run. This is bounded compatibility evidence, not an independent whole-repository certification.
No holdout, GPU, provider, external service or host-process discovery was used. Tests used private SQLite files and ordinary connection-level operations.
